title: The remote_ajax_refs feature added an ajax_lookup endpoint that skipped both the login and is_accessible checks enforced on all other admin routes.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The new ajax_lookup endpoint (sqladmin/application.py:519-537) returns model rows from a user-controlled identity/name/term without any authentication or authorization check. findings.explanation: The new ajax_lookup endpoint (sqladmin/application.py:519-537) returns model rows from a user-controlled identity/name/term without any authentication or authorization check. Every other data-returning admin endpoint (index, list, details, delete, create, edit, export) is decorated with @login_required (lines 340, 346, 371, 392, 409, 444, 483), and the sibling export endpoint additionally enforces model_view.is_accessible(request) via _export (lines 225-228). ajax_lookup has neither @login_required nor an is_accessible check, so when an AuthenticationBackend is configured, an unauthenticated caller can enumerate and read model data. This violates the documented model where is_accessible 'controls if this Model/View should be accessed' and where the backend's authenticate() 'will be called for each incoming request to validate the authentication'.

evidence.content:
async def ajax_lookup(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        """Ajax lookup route."""

        identity = request.path_params["identity"]
        model_view = self._find_model_view(identity)

        name = request.query_params.get("name")
        term = request.query_params.get("term")

        if not name or not term:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400)

        try:
            loader: QueryAjaxModelLoader = model_view._form_ajax_refs[name]
        except KeyError:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400)

        data = [loader.format(m) for m in await loader.get_list(term)]
        return JSONResponse({"results": data})

@login_required
    async def export(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        """Export model endpoint."""

        await self._export(request)

        identity = request.path_params["identity"]
        export_type = request.path_params["export_type"]

        model_view = self._find_model_view(identity)
        rows = await model_view.get_model_objects(limit=model_view.export_max_rows)
        return model_view.export_data(rows, export_type=export_type)

async def _export(self, request: Request) -> None:
        model_view = self._find_model_view(request.path_params["identity"])
        if not model_view.can_export or not model_view.is_accessible(request):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403)

findings.suggested_fix: Decorate ajax_lookup with @login_required and add an authorization guard (e.g. `if not model_view.is_accessible(request): raise HTTPException(status_code=403)`) before returning data, mirroring the export/_export pattern.
